name: 15a perplexity walkthrough
title: Perplexity is the exponential of the average loss per token
subtitle: Section 2 example: "the cat sat" with next token probabilities 0.2, 0.1 and 0.3; natural log, so losses are in nats

steps.caption: Score the sentence one position at a time. At each step the model has already produced a full distribution, and we read off only the probability of the token that really came next.
At the start of text the model gave "the" probability 0.2. The loss is minus the natural log, -ln 0.2 = 1.609 nats.
After "the" it gave "cat" only 0.1, so this position costs 2.303 nats, the largest surprise in the sentence.
After "the cat" it gave "sat" 0.3, costing 1.204 nats. The total is 5.116 nats and the sentence probability is 0.2 × 0.1 × 0.3 = 0.006.

The loss averages 1.705 nats over the 3 tokens, and exponentiating that average gives the perplexity. Perplexity 5.50 means the model was as uncertain as a fair choice among about 5.5 tokens at each step.
A model that spreads probability evenly over the whole vocabulary pays ln 32,000 = 10.37 nats on every token, so its perplexity is the vocabulary size. Real models start training near this number.
